title: Old vs new tax regime for 2026-27: how to choose for your salary

faq.question: Which tax regime is better for a ₹15 lakh salary?
faq.answer: At ₹15 lakh the new regime charges ₹97,500 including cess. The old regime only matches that if you have about ₹5.44 lakh in deductions and exemptions beyond the standard deduction, typically a large HRA plus the ₹1.5 lakh investment deduction and health insurance, or a home loan. Without rent or a home loan, the new regime usually wins.

faq.question: Is the new regime always better below ₹12.75 lakh?
faq.answer: Almost always. A salary up to ₹12.75 lakh pays no tax in the new regime, thanks to the ₹75,000 standard deduction and the rebate up to ₹12 lakh of taxable income. To pay zero under the old regime you'd need deductions of ₹4.5 lakh at ₹10 lakh and over ₹7 lakh at ₹12.75 lakh.

faq.question: Does the 50% HRA rule apply in the new regime?
faq.answer: No. HRA exemption, including the higher 50% rate now available in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad, is available only under the old regime. The same goes for the higher meal, education and hostel allowance limits from April 2026.

faq.question: Can I switch regimes every year?
faq.answer: If you have no business income, yes: you can choose the regime each year, and the final choice is made when you file your return. Different rules apply if you have business income, so check those separately. Tell your employer your choice at the start of the year so the right amount of TDS is deducted.

faq.question: What if my deductions are close to the break-even?
faq.answer: Then the difference in tax is small, and other factors matter more: the new regime needs no investment proofs and draws less scrutiny of HRA claims. Run the numbers with your actual figures, and if the old regime saves only a few thousand rupees, many people reasonably choose the simpler option.
